detail.body:
## Overview

Publish completed iteration records over ZeroMQ using the existing FPM v1 contract. #52061 retains its original review history; timing and workload collection now live in transport-independent parents.

Dependency order: #61690 (timing) → #61691 (workload) → **#52061 (FPM exporter)**. The stack is independent of, and complementary to, #61424; that PR is not a prerequisite. [Previous layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61691) · [Review only this layer](https://github.com/tedzhouhk/vllm/compare/5c733548955e31fb37ec819f200d675f953db432...eba027b00bcabf6009cb906ef804b7f3ed441ed6) · [Pre-split head](https://github.com/tedzhouhk/vllm/tree/hzhou-codex/fpm-before-stack-20261014).

All three retain their PR numbers/reviews and target `main`, so downstream upstream-facing diffs are cumulative. Review the layer-only comparisons and merge/rebase in order. This update moves workload ownership into PR2; the exporter contract is unchanged.

## Claims

- Optional, default-off `--forward-pass-metrics-port` derives workload/timing without verbose logging or Prometheus statistics. There is no separate timing switch.
- Schema, mapping, encoding and publisher utilities remain together in `vllm/v1/metrics/forward_pass_metrics.py`. Wire `version=1` and field names are unchanged. Internal milliseconds convert to `wall_time` seconds only here; `counter_id` is publication sequence, not iteration ID.
- Each EngineCore enqueues complete records before frontend attachment, including when an existing stats owner is reused. Its dedicated CPU publisher thread converts, encodes and sends independently of Python, native-Rust or offline frontend consumption. With `uni`, the thread shares the GPU driver's process/GIL; `mp` workers are separate.
- One socket per EngineCore binds at `base + global DP index`. Threads start after workers initialize, elastic new engines bind during initialization, and port conflicts fail startup.
- Independent subscribers support streaming or latest-value sampling. The example in `examples/features/forward_pass_metrics/` accepts `--port`, uses `--interval 0` for streaming and defaults to one-second latest display within two 80-character lines.

Compared with Dynamo's [InstrumentedScheduler](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/components/src/dynamo/vllm/instrumented_scheduler.py), this path joins native workload snapshots with direct GPU timing; no custom scheduler or scheduler-derived duration is needed. Self-benchmark orchestration remains in Dynamo. The exporter does not duplicate the parent APIs or prevent a future OTLP exporter. Related proposals: #38760, #39979, #61423.

## Validation

Current head: `eba027b00bcabf6009cb906ef804b7f3ed441ed6`, on workload parent `5c733548955e31fb37ec819f200d675f953db432`.

127 focused full-stack tests passed, as did normal hooks/mypy and independent review. The existing ownership regression checks preserved LoRA enrichment and exactly-once exporter submission for absent, zero and nonzero frontend owners. Exporter submission stays before the ownership early return. The FPM protocol module and subscriber are byte-identical to `b1be451060`.

Two pinned-source RTX 6000 Ada cases passed with MRV2 async eager TP1/PP1 and UniProc: workload-only and FPM, both with actual `log_stats=False`, no custom logger or iteration log lines. Each delivered 48 positive timings before shutdown and matched the fresh PR1 timing-off token baseline. Independent verification checked 96 raw/generic millisecond matches, all four workload/top-level count equalities, and every active FPM duration and workload field. The capture contained 48 active plus two idle frames; startup idle counter zero is not claimed captured. Both engines exited cleanly and the GPU was cleared. No failed GPU attempt, harness timeout, new throughput or multi-GPU qualification is claimed.

## Details

The PUB envelope matches [KV events](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_events.py): topic, eight-byte big-endian sequence and MessagePack payload. There is no replay service, acknowledgement or retained history.

`model_step_cuda` covers execution, sampling/drafting and host-submission gaps on the recorded stream. PP reports only the last-stage output worker, possibly including upstream-input waits—not whole-pipeline latency. Zero means EngineCore-confirmed idle; timed dummy records have empty scheduled work and may contain queued work. Prefill variance still uses `kv_read + scheduled_tokens/2`, without renaming the v1 field.

Delivery is best effort: bounded queues, ZMQ high-water marks, startup, disconnects and shutdown can drop records. Local drops are logged; later sequences may expose gaps, but tail loss may not. CPU/IPC overhead needs representative measurement. Sockets bind all interfaces without authentication and require a trusted network.

Support requires generative CUDA models, `uni`/`mp` executors and out-of-process EngineCore; unsupported required timing is rejected. Historical multi-GPU limitations remain recorded below.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex. Existing review replies/resolutions remain for the human author; the broader parent polling/architecture discussion remains open.

<details>
<summary>Previous validation — before frontend-ownership and drain-lock fixes (b1be4510)</summary>

Current head: `b1be451060746ea61dcaf7a9e2c50f55553ec8ff`, on workload parent `cca105bfb2767cc728afcc36701c98cde28abbc5`.

125 focused full-stack tests passed, including the FPM v1 wire contract, subscriber formatting, async-output preservation, timing association and FIFO readiness. Normal pre-commit/mypy passed. The FPM production module and subscriber are byte-identical to the previous exporter head `9b41592984`; its existing wire fixture now names workload fields explicitly.

Two pinned-source RTX 6000 Ada full-stack cases passed with MRV2 async eager TP1/PP1 and UniProc inside EngineCoreProc: workload-only and FPM, both with actual `log_stats=False`, no custom logger and no iteration log lines. Each delivered 48 positive timings before shutdown, with exact worker-ms/generic-ms and baseline-token parity. The FPM subscriber captured 50 v1 frames (48 active, two idle); every active duration and scheduled/queued field matched the complete generic record. This does not claim capture of the first startup idle frame. Both engines exited cleanly and the GPU was cleared.

An outdated external observer initially failed on duplicate count keys. That attempt is retained; only the corrected rerun pair is qualified. Independent verification checks count consistency, wire fields and unit conversion. No production workaround or performance claim is made.

Focused reproduction:

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_forward_pass_metrics.py -q
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --forward-pass-metrics-port 20380 --disable-log-stats
python examples/features/forward_pass_metrics/forward_pass_metrics_subscriber.py \
  --port 20380 --interval 0
```

Previous functional and overhead results are preserved below at their actual source heads and configurations. They are not current-head reruns or evidence of fresh CI, throughput or multi-GPU qualification.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Previous top-level validation — pre-restack head e0df2bd5</summary>

This text is retained from the description at `e0df2bd582e44ceddcfc1fb5d772d98d0e33f1b8`. References to the current head or campaign below refer to that earlier revision, not the timing-only restack.

Head `e0df2bd5`: 124 focused tests, normal hooks/mypy and independent review passed. A known-value probe through real timer/output/collector/encoder classes verified immediate, delayed and dummy-sample paths: 12.5ms internal timing becomes 0.0125s on the encoded v1 wire.

Eight pinned-source RTX 6000 Ada GPU cases passed: six parent timing off/on cases and two full-stack workload/FPM cases. The full-stack cases used MRV2 async eager TP1/PP1 with UniProc, actual `log_stats=False`, no custom logger and zero iteration logs. Each returned 48 positive timings. FPM emitted 50 v1 frames (48 active, two idle); all active workload fields and `wall_time == elapsed_ms * 0.001` matched. Across the campaign, all 208 worker samples exactly matched generic milliseconds. Workers exited cleanly and the GPU was cleared. No new throughput or multi-GPU claim is made.

Independent focused reproduction (6 passed):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor.py::test_iteration_timing_poll_preserves_model_response_order \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_engine_logger_apis.py::test_iteration_logging_preserves_records_without_inventing_timing \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_forward_pass_metrics.py::test_iteration_mapping_preserves_fpm_v1_wire_contract \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

This revision includes PR1 readability fixes and millisecond-to-second conversion at the FPM boundary. Earlier checks/overhead measurements are collapsed below with their actual SHAs/configurations; none is a current-head throughput rerun. Current KV usage is removed only from historical per-iteration logs, not periodic reporting.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier qualification — original source SHAs and limitations</summary>

### Start/cancel guard restack

Includes parent #61690's same-file start/cancel guard refinement (`07f80ade`); this layer is a patch-identical replay. The full-stack delta only changes the worker guard and one existing zero-token test parameter. 99 focused PR1 tests, 124 focused full-stack tests, normal hooks/mypy and independent review passed. Current parent GPU validation is described in #61690; previous multi-GPU and performance results below remain pinned to their original heads.

### Code-ablation restack (`970c638f`)

Includes parent #61690's smaller timer/worker/RPC implementation and clearer derived-state name. Exporter, wire schema and workload/idle behavior are unchanged; this layer's replay only adapts the internal-name assertion. The complete stack is 23 lines smaller (19 production lines), with no added test cases. This head passed 123 focused tests, 115 existing argument regressions, normal hooks/mypy and independent review. The parent's four actual-multiprocessing GPU cases passed, including native MTP with exact off/on tokens. Earlier Compute Lab and performance evidence below remains pinned to its original heads; no new throughput or multi-GPU claim is made.

Two pinned-source RTX 6000 Ada cases on this full-stack head also passed with actual `log_stats=False`, no custom logger and zero iteration log lines: workload-only and FPM each returned all 48 positive timings. FPM emitted 50 frames (48 active, two idle), with all active fields/durations matching generic records and correct v1 schema/counters. These used MRV2 async eager, TP1/PP1 and UniProc; they are correctness checks, not throughput measurements.

### Earlier refinement qualification (`80bb05d2`)

79 focused tests and 136 additional existing argument, scheduler, SHM, auxiliary-output, and executor regressions passed on this full-stack head; suite counts overlap. Normal hooks and independent review passed. Local workload-only and FPM tests with actual `log_stats=False` returned 48 positive timings without iteration logs; the FPM test matched all active durations and fields on the v1 wire.

Compute Lab job `5035162` used four A100-SXM4-40GB GPUs. PP2 native MTP (MRV2 async eager) passed all 32 workload/timing/wire checks and exact baseline token parity. A validation-only 5-second drain hold recovered all 48 PP2 timings after final token output, with exact FPM mapping. DP2 x PP2 / EP2 async/sync runs at synchronization interval 64 emitted 6,162/5,656 wire records: 6,146/5,634 timed records, including 4,599/4,087 dummy records, plus 16/22 idle records. The offline audit matched every generic/wire pair, per-worker sequences, schema v1, durations and scheduled/queued fields. Each DP replica had only one last-stage timer; there were zero active-wave timing polls. Skewed/bursty traffic, queued prefill, delayed dummy timing and pause/resume were exercised.

These are observer-instrumented correctness checks, not new throughput results. DP output/oracle checks completed before shutdown, but worker teardown required force-kill. Native-MTP PP2 is qualified here only for MRV2 async eager; other attempted combinations failed on the old timing-off baseline as documented in #61690. The remote custom record logger enables log stats, so only the separate local tests above establish `log_stats=False` behavior.

### Earlier test-minimality and readability validation

Test-minimality follow-up `75066a76` reduces redundant field/width permutations and refresh repetitions while retaining FPM v1 wire, configuration, dummy/idle, backpressure, lifecycle, and stream/sample contracts. All 13 exporter cases passed. Across the stack, the audited introduced/renamed cases were reduced from 94 to 70; all 70 plus four extended existing cases passed together (74 total), with normal hooks passing. Only tests changed; production code and docs match `ff85031b`. No new GPU/performance run is claimed.

Readability restack `a4658cc5`: includes parent #61690's worker-helper cleanup (`44f6fa12`); this layer's exporter patch is unchanged, verified by `git range-diff`. 102 focused tests passed on this head, including exporter/serialization and worker timing regressions; normal hooks passed. The parent's eight local GPU smoke cases validate the identical timing helpers. No new exporter GPU, multi-GPU, or throughput qualification is claimed.

### Earlier automatic-enablement validation

Earlier automatic-enablement head `3991bddb`: 203 focused tests plus three in-process client-guard cases passed; normal hooks passed. The parent changes remove the public timing flag and derive timing from consumers. FPM still enables workload and timing without verbose logs, independently of `log_stats`. A that-head Qwen3-0.6B MRV2 smoke on RTX 6000 Ada (eager, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, FlashInfer sampler JIT disabled) produced 48 timed records and 50 wire frames. Every timed frame matched the generic duration and scheduled/queued fields; log statistics were disabled, no iteration log lines were printed, and output tokens matched the same-runner baseline. The timer, collector, exporter, scheduler, worker/executor, Rust, and example implementations are unchanged from `af574626`; the prior full campaign below is not relabeled as a that-head rerun.

### Earlier full Compute Lab qualification

Self-review caught a compatibility regression in the first split: a publisher owned only by Python `MPClient` is never created by the native Rust frontend, which talks directly to headless EngineCore. This revision restores engine-owned publication while continuing to consume the generic completed records from the parent PRs. It removes the frontend-specific hooks and multi-rank publisher machinery rather than duplicating the wire implementation in Rust.

Previously qualified standalone head `af574626` passed 592 relevant regression tests, 22 selected client tests, and both SHM readiness/overflow cases (616 total), with zero failures/skips. One PP3 case was explicitly deselected on the two-GPU allocation; heavy gated-model client E2Es were not selected. Normal hooks, upstream pre-commit, and upstream docs passed on that head; full upstream Buildkite was not triggered. Tests cover FPM v1 mapping, global DP identity, socket lifecycle, bounded queue loss, and exactly-once enqueueing rather than guaranteed delivery.

Compute Lab functional qualification used A100-SXM4-40GB GPUs, CUDA PyTorch 2.13/cu130, and the published native wheel/Rust binary matching upstream base `e96c82266`. All cases below used `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`; DP and UniProc MTP exercised CUDA graphs, while native Rust, multi-frontend, and offline probes used eager execution. These are observer-instrumented correctness checks, not overhead measurements.

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Native `vllm-rs` headless HTTP/gRPC, actual UniProc executor | Seven HTTP requests plus one real gRPC request; 55 timed + 3 idle FPM, matching all generic fields and expected 225 prefill tokens/80 decode positions. No Python MPClient construction or `core_client` import. |
| Native Rust negative control, frontend-owned `da2d58a3` | Same requests and generic metrics succeeded, but no FPM port was bound and zero frames arrived. The fixed engine-owned version passed the same harness. |
| PowerMoE-3b DP2/EP2, MRV2 sync scheduler, sync interval 64 | 19 requests, 2,946 timed records including 1,453 dummy, 18 idle. All 2,964 wire frames matched generic records; no observed sequence gaps, no false idle, no active-wave timing polls. Pending associations peaked at 22. |
| Two API frontends; late/concurrent/reconnecting subscribers | 32 HTTP requests split 16/16; all 136 timed records matched the 144-frame primary stream, with no observed gaps. EngineCore was the sole publisher. Overlapping subscriber payloads and periodic latest sampling matched. |
| Actual offline `LLM.generate`, SyncMP client, UniProc | 48 output tokens; 17 timed + 4 idle FPM. No extra engine steps were needed for subsequent idle records, and the offline output queue remained empty. All timed records were already present at return in this run; it does not demonstrate a delayed timed tail. |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B native MTP + FPM, UniProc, both runners | Each returned 32 timed records with exact wire/context parity. MRV1 accepted 70/81 draft tokens; MRV2 accepted 72/84. One startup/idle record per run was not observed over PUB/SUB; all timed records arrived. |

The parent PRs report standalone timing/workload, TP2, prefix-cache reuse, MRV1/MRV2 × sync/async, and DP+MTP flow qualification. The full-stack cases in this earlier campaign ran at `af574626`; all evidence remains scoped to its actual source and configuration.

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS='' python -m pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_forward_pass_metrics.py -q
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --forward-pass-metrics-port 20380 --disable-log-stats
python examples/features/forward_pass_metrics/forward_pass_metrics_subscriber.py --port 20380
python examples/features/forward_pass_metrics/forward_pass_metrics_subscriber.py --port 20380 --interval 0
```

### Earlier controlled overhead (`af574626`)

The clean campaign passed all 21 engine launches and 84 measurement windows: three launches per MP arm (dependency-base off, final off, timing only, workload, FPM), plus three alternating UniProc off/FPM pairs. Configuration: Qwen3-0.6B, one A100, bf16, MRV2 async, CUDA graphs, prefix cache/log statistics off, 32 running sequences and a 2,048-token batch budget. Each launch warmed every traffic shape twice, then measured each for at least ten seconds. CPU affinity was identical between arms; the subscriber used a separate reserved core. No per-iteration observers or synchronization debugger ran during measurement; no measured-phase compilation was detected. Every FPM window remained active, with no observed sequence gaps/duplicates and actual mixed-traffic queue pressure.

Throughput changes below are the median of three paired per-round ratios, with [minimum, maximum]. The baseline is the same final head with FPM/timing/workload disabled. Decode/mixed use output-token throughput; prefill uses total-token throughput.

| Traffic (prompt/output tokens) | MP FPM/off | UniProc FPM/off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decode c1, 128/256 | −0.41% [−0.49, −0.38] | −0.31% [−0.41, −0.29] |
| Decode c32, 128/256 | −0.53% [−0.86, −0.44] | −0.32% [−0.40, −0.14] |
| Prefill c32, 2048/1 | +0.02% [+0.00, +0.20] | +0.07% [−0.16, +0.10] |
| Mixed c64, alternating 32/256 and 1024/32 | −0.53% [−0.90, −0.53] | −0.32% [−0.61, +0.04] |

Final-off versus dependency-base off had paired median throughput changes between −0.19% and +0.18% across these shapes. The first-round decode32 TTFT p50 difference (+10.65 ms) did not persist at that magnitude: later rounds were +1.67 and −0.84 ms. The timing-only arm on the final stack changed throughput by −0.41%, +0.04%, +0.03%, and −0.79%, respectively; these are feature-flag comparisons, not standalone-parent performance runs.

This is not zero overhead or a universal sub-percent latency claim. For MP, FPM-on increases c1 ITL p99 by a paired median 0.10 ms (+4.13%) and decode32 TTFT p99 by 3.23 ms (+5.95%). UniProc c1 ITL p99 increases 0.027 ms (+1.08%); its decode32 TTFT p99 median decreases 0.72 ms. Results are limited to this small-model, single-GPU closed-loop campaign with three repeats and unlocked GPU clocks; they do not establish AgentX, DP, or production-scale overhead. Earlier AgentX/microbenchmark results retain their original pinned pre-refactor scope.

</details>

@@ -306,6 +306,46 @@ every 5 seconds with some key metrics:
   seconds
 - The prefix cache hit rate over the most recent 1k kv-cache block queries
 
+`--enable-logging-iteration-details` additionally logs per-iteration request and
+token counts. With log statistics enabled, it automatically includes GPU timing
+for CUDA generation with a `uni` or `mp` executor and an out-of-process
+EngineCore; unsupported configurations log counts only. This logging option is
+disabled by default, and there is no separate timing CLI flag.
+
+The `model_step_cuda` duration covers target-model execution, sampling and
+postprocessing, and drafting for the next iteration on the recorded CUDA stream,
+including CPU submission gaps. It excludes independent work on other streams and
+is not end-to-end request latency. With pipeline parallelism, only the output
+worker of the last stage is timed. Its interval may include waiting for input
+from earlier stages; it is not the duration of the whole pipeline.
+
+### Iteration Workload Metrics
+
+`--enable-iteration-workload-metrics` automatically enables GPU timing without
+turning on iteration logging. It adds scheduled logical KV-context sums and
+per-request population variances, plus a waiting-work snapshot. Unlike logging,
+this feature requires a configuration supported by GPU timing. The scheduled
+prefill variance uses
+`kv_context + scheduled_tokens / 2` for each request; decode variance uses the
+prior context length. These are logical token lengths, not physical KV cache
+occupancy or measured memory traffic. Scheduling phase is inherited from the
+scheduler, including prefill recomputation after preemption.
+
+Queued work is captured after output processing (at submission for dummy steps).
+For compatibility with FPM consumers, preempted requests and requests waiting
+for remote KV are grouped as queued decode; other waiting requests are grouped
+as queued prefill. This queue classification is distinct from execution phase.
+Deferred requests are already included in the two waiting queues and are not
+counted again. Speculative rejection corrects only later context snapshots from
+the same request/preemption generation, not the original scheduled-token counts.
+
+When workload collection is enabled, EngineCore sends explicit idle records at
+one-second intervals only while globally idle and after outstanding timings have
+been collected. Dummy executions remain timed model iterations, not idle records.
+Idle snapshots may retain queued work while scheduling is paused. Workload
+collection is disabled by default, so ordinary serving does not scan these
+queues or emit periodic idle snapshots.
+
 ### Metrics Publishing - Prometheus
 
 The `PrometheusStatLogger` metrics publisher makes the metrics

@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+# Forward-Pass Metrics
+
+Forward-pass metrics (FPM) export one completed engine iteration at a time for
+external performance modeling and orchestration. The feature is optional and
+disabled by default.
+
+## Enable and subscribe
+
+```bash
+vllm serve MODEL --forward-pass-metrics-port 20380
+
+python examples/features/forward_pass_metrics/forward_pass_metrics_subscriber.py \
+    --port 20380
+```
+
+The port flag enables iteration GPU timing and workload collection. It does not
+enable verbose iteration logging and works with `--disable-log-stats`.
+Use `--forward-pass-metrics-worker-id` to override the default vLLM instance ID.
+
+Data-parallel rank `N` publishes on `BASE_PORT + N` on its **EngineCore host**.
+Each engine owns one publisher, independently of the number or implementation
+of API frontends. Python serving, offline clients, and native Rust frontends
+(`vllm-rs serve`) use the same publication path. Ports bind during engine
+initialization, including when elastic scaling starts a new engine.
+
+Subscribers can join and leave independently of the engine. By default, the
+example displays the latest record once per second while validating every
+received message. Use `--interval 0` to display the full stream, or
+`--interval 5` to display the latest record every five seconds. Each record
+occupies at most two 80-character lines.
+
+## Record semantics
+
+The engine matches the scheduling snapshot and GPU timing by iteration ID
+before handing a complete record to the exporter. The exporter does not read
+scheduler state, calculate CUDA timing, or reconstruct associations.
+
+The FPM v1 schema is defined in
+[`vllm/v1/metrics/forward_pass_metrics.py`](../../vllm/v1/metrics/forward_pass_metrics.py).
+Its main fields are:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `worker_id`, `dp_rank` | Engine identity and data-parallel rank. |
+| `counter_id` | Per-rank publication sequence; distinct from the internal iteration ID. |
+| `timing_scope` | `model_step_cuda`: model execution, sampling, and speculative drafting on the recorded CUDA stream, including host-submission gaps. |
+| `wall_time` | CUDA interval in seconds; zero is reserved for engine-confirmed idle. |
+| `scheduled_requests` | Prefill/decode request counts, token/context-length sums, and population variances. |
+| `queued_requests` | Waiting prefill/decode work captured by the iteration-metrics collector. |
+
+With pipeline parallelism, timing comes from the output worker of the last
+stage. It may include waiting for input from earlier stages, but does not
+measure the whole pipeline or independent work on other CUDA streams.
+
+Prefill length variance uses each request's
+`kv_read + scheduled_tokens / 2`. Decode KV statistics describe logical context
+lengths, not the number of input tokens scheduled in that iteration.
+
+A data-parallel dummy iteration has measured timing and empty scheduled
+metrics; queued metrics may be nonempty. Only the engine's explicitly confirmed
+idle state produces a zero-duration heartbeat. Silence from a publisher does
+not imply idle.
+
+## Transport and overhead
+
+The publisher uses the same three-frame ZeroMQ PUB envelope as KV events:
+an empty topic, an eight-byte big-endian sequence number, and a MessagePack
+payload. Unlike the KV-event publisher, it does not provide a replay socket.
+
+EngineCore enqueues complete records without waiting for subscribers. A
+background thread performs conversion, encoding, and socket operations,
+including after the last request output. No frontend output consumption is
+required. Adding subscribers does not add CUDA events or scheduler collection
+work.
+
+Delivery is best effort: the bounded queue, ZeroMQ high-water marks, startup
+subscription handshakes, disconnects, and shutdown can drop records. Local
+queue drops and bind failures are logged; sequence gaps reveal some losses.
+There is no historical replay or acknowledgement from subscribers. Port
+conflicts fail engine startup instead of silently disabling FPM.
+
+Publication adds CPU overhead in addition to iteration collection.
+Benchmark the complete enabled path with representative traffic; background
+publication is not a zero-overhead guarantee.
+
+FPM inherits the iteration timer's current restrictions: generative CUDA
+models, `uni` or `mp` executors, and a multiprocessing EngineCore client.
+Ordinary single-GPU serving is supported;
+in-process EngineCore mode (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) is not.
+
+!!! warning
+    The publisher binds all network interfaces and has no authentication.
+    Expose its ports only on a trusted network.

@@ -0,0 +1,254 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Subscribe to native vLLM forward-pass metrics.
+
+Start vLLM with FPM enabled before running this script:
+
+    vllm serve MODEL --forward-pass-metrics-port 20380
+    python forward_pass_metrics_subscriber.py --port 20380
+
+For data parallel deployments, each EngineCore publishes rank N on
+BASE_PORT + N. Connect to that engine's host and run one subscriber per rank
+endpoint.
+
+By default, display the latest sample once per second, while receiving and
+validating every message. Use --interval 0 to print every iteration. Displayed
+sequence numbers can therefore skip without indicating a gap in the stream.
+
+Example output (S=scheduled, Q=queued; variances are in tokens squared):
+
+           seq step_ms   prefill:req/tok/kv/var      decode:req/kv/var
+             7      12 S 2/8/6/1                     2/64/0
+                      Q 1/12/-/0                    0/0/0
+
+Each sample occupies at most two lines of at most 80 characters. Large values
+use scientific notation; '-' means not applicable. The Q row is omitted when
+the queue is empty. Worker identity and timing scope are printed separately
+when they change.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import math
+import sys
+import time
+from textwrap import fill
+
+import msgspec
+import zmq
+
+from vllm.v1.metrics.forward_pass_metrics import (
+    FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA,
+    FPM_VERSION,
+    ForwardPassMetrics,
+)
+
+POLL_TIMEOUT_MS = 1000
+DISPLAY_WIDTH = 80
+HEADER = (
+    f"{'seq':>10} {'step_ms':>7}   {'prefill:req/tok/kv/var':<27} decode:req/kv/var"
+)
+
+
+def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Subscribe to native vLLM forward-pass metrics.",
+        formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter,
+    )
+    address = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
+    address.add_argument(
+        "--endpoint",
+        help="ZMQ endpoint for one vLLM data-parallel rank.",
+    )
+    address.add_argument(
+        "--port",
+        type=int,
+        default=20380,
+        help="Local FPM port (shorthand for --endpoint tcp://localhost:PORT).",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--interval",
+        type=float,
+        default=1.0,
+        help="Seconds between latest-sample displays; 0 prints every iteration.",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if not 1 <= args.port <= 65535:
+        parser.error("--port must be between 1 and 65535")
+    if not math.isfinite(args.interval) or args.interval < 0:
+        parser.error("--interval must be finite and nonnegative")
+    args.endpoint = args.endpoint or f"tcp://localhost:{args.port}"
+    return args
+
+
+def compact(value: int | float) -> str:
+    """Fit one number in six columns, preserving small integer counts exactly."""
+    if isinstance(value, int) and len(str(value)) <= 6:
+        return str(value)
+    for precision in (3, 2, 1):
+        text = f"{value:.{precision}g}".replace("e+", "e").replace("e-0", "e-")
+        if len(text) <= 6:
+            return text
+    return text
+
+
+def print_metrics(sequence: int, metrics: ForwardPassMetrics) -> None:
+    prefix = f"{sequence:>10} {compact(metrics.wall_time * 1000):>7}"
+    idle = metrics.wall_time == 0.0
+    if idle:
+        print(f"{sequence:>10} {'-':>7}   idle (heartbeat)", flush=True)
+        prefix = " " * len(prefix)
+    for label, counts, prefill_kv in (
+        (
+            "S",
+            metrics.scheduled_requests,
+            compact(metrics.scheduled_requests.sum_prefill_kv_tokens),
+        ),
+        ("Q", metrics.queued_requests, "-"),
+    ):
+        if idle and label == "S":
+            continue
+        if label == "Q" and not (
+            counts.num_prefill_requests or counts.num_decode_requests
+        ):
+            continue
+        prefill = "/".join(
+            (
+                compact(counts.num_prefill_requests),
+                compact(counts.sum_prefill_tokens),
+                prefill_kv,
+                compact(counts.var_prefill_length),
+            )
+        )
+        decode = "/".join(
+            compact(value)
+            for value in (
+                counts.num_decode_requests,
+                counts.sum_decode_kv_tokens,
+                counts.var_decode_kv_tokens,
+            )
+        )
+        print(f"{prefix} {label} {prefill:<27} {decode}", flush=True)
+        prefix = " " * len(prefix)
+
+
+class MetricsDisplay:
+    """Coalesce display updates without skipping validation of received messages."""
+
+    def __init__(self, interval: float):
+        self.interval = interval
+        self.next_print = 0.0
+        self.pending: tuple[int, ForwardPassMetrics] | None = None
+        self.identity: tuple[str, int, str] | None = None
+
+    def update(self, sequence: int, metrics: ForwardPassMetrics) -> None:
+        self.pending = sequence, metrics
+        self.flush()
+
+    def poll_timeout_ms(self) -> int:
+        if self.pending is None:
+            return POLL_TIMEOUT_MS
+        remaining_ms = math.ceil((self.next_print - time.monotonic()) * 1000)
+        return max(0, min(POLL_TIMEOUT_MS, remaining_ms))
+
+    def flush(self, *, force: bool = False) -> None:
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if self.pending is None or (not force and now < self.next_print):
+            return
+        sequence, metrics = self.pending
+        identity = metrics.worker_id, metrics.dp_rank, metrics.timing_scope
+        if identity != self.identity:
+            print(
+                fill(
+                    f"worker={ascii(metrics.worker_id)} dp={metrics.dp_rank} "
+                    f"scope={metrics.timing_scope}",
+                    width=DISPLAY_WIDTH,
+                )
+            )
+            print(HEADER)
+            self.identity = identity
+        print_metrics(sequence, metrics)
+        self.pending = None
+        self.next_print = now + self.interval
+
+
+def warn(message: str) -> None:
+    print(fill(message, width=DISPLAY_WIDTH), file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    args = parse_args()
+    decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(ForwardPassMetrics)
+    context = zmq.Context()
+    subscriber = context.socket(zmq.SUB)
+    subscriber.connect(args.endpoint)
+    subscriber.setsockopt(zmq.SUBSCRIBE, b"")
+    last_sequence: int | None = None
+    display = MetricsDisplay(args.interval)
+
+    print(fill(f"FPM {args.endpoint} | Ctrl-C to stop", width=DISPLAY_WIDTH))
+    print(
+        "Every iteration (no display throttling)"
+        if args.interval == 0
+        else fill(
+            f"Latest sample every {args.interval:g}s; "
+            "all messages checked (display skips are normal).",
+            width=DISPLAY_WIDTH,
+        )
+    )
+    print(
+        "S=scheduled; Q=queued (when nonempty); tok/kv=tokens; var=tokens^2; -=n/a",
+        flush=True,
+    )
+    try:
+        while True:
+            display.flush()
+            if not subscriber.poll(display.poll_timeout_ms()):
+                continue
+
+            frames = subscriber.recv_multipart()
+            if len(frames) != 3:
+                warn(f"Ignoring message with {len(frames)} frames; expected 3")
+                continue
+
+            topic, sequence_bytes, payload = frames
+            if topic or len(sequence_bytes) != 8:
+                warn("Ignoring malformed FPM envelope")
+                continue
+
+            sequence = int.from_bytes(sequence_bytes, "big")
+            try:
+                metrics = decoder.decode(payload)
+            except msgspec.DecodeError as error:
+                warn(f"Ignoring malformed FPM payload: {error}")
+                continue
+
+            if metrics.version != FPM_VERSION:
+                warn(f"Ignoring FPM version {metrics.version}; expected {FPM_VERSION}")
+                continue
+            if metrics.timing_scope != FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA:
+                warn(
+                    f"Ignoring timing scope {metrics.timing_scope!r}; "
+                    f"expected {FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA!r}"
+                )
+                continue
+            if metrics.counter_id != sequence:
+                warn(
+                    f"Envelope sequence {sequence} does not match payload counter "
+                    f"{metrics.counter_id}"
+                )
+            if last_sequence is not None and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
+                warn(f"Sequence gap: previous={last_sequence}, current={sequence}")
+
+            display.update(sequence, metrics)
+            last_sequence = sequence
+    except KeyboardInterrupt:
+        display.flush(force=True)
+        print("Stopped.")
+    finally:
+        subscriber.close(linger=0)
+        context.term()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+def test_ready_events_are_reused_without_waiting_for_pending_or_contended_drains():
+    events = [Mock() for _ in range(4)]
+    events[0].elapsed_time.return_value = 7.0
+    events[1].query.return_value = False
+    events[2].elapsed_time.return_value = 8.0
+    events[3].query.return_value = True
+    timer = IterationTimer(2, event_factory=iter(events).__next__)
+    timer.start(4)
+    timer.finish()
+
+    assert timer.drain_samples() == ()
+    events[0].elapsed_time.assert_not_called()
+    events[1].query.return_value = True
+    with timer._drain_lock:
+        assert timer.drain_samples() == ()
+
+    def append_during_query():
+        events[1].query.side_effect = None
+        timer.start(5)
+        timer.finish()
+        return True
+
+    events[1].query.side_effect = append_during_query
+    assert timer.drain_samples() == ((4, 7.0), (5, 8.0))
+
+    # The factory is exhausted; the next intervals must reuse the ready pairs.
+    timer.start(6)
+    timer.finish()
+    timer.start(7)
+    timer.finish()
+    assert timer.drain_samples() == ((6, 7.0), (7, 8.0))
+    for event in events:
+        assert event.record.call_count == 2

+def _decode_workload_output(lengths: dict[str, int]) -> SchedulerOutput:
+    output = SchedulerOutput.make_empty()
+    output.num_scheduled_tokens = dict.fromkeys(lengths, 4)
+    output.total_num_scheduled_tokens = len(lengths) * 4
+    output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens = {rid: [-1] * 3 for rid in lengths}
+    cached = output.scheduled_cached_reqs
+    cached.req_ids = list(lengths)
+    cached.num_computed_tokens = list(lengths.values())
+    cached.num_output_tokens = [1] * len(lengths)
+    cached.prefill_req_ids = set()
+    workload = IterationWorkloadAccumulator()
+    for length in lengths.values():
+        workload.add_decode(length, 4)
+    output.scheduled_workload = workload.snapshot()
+    return output

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""FPM v1 wire format and export of completed engine iteration records.
+
+Timing, workload snapshots, and input/time association belong to the generic
+iteration-metrics pipeline. This module only maps its completed records and
+publishes them from a bounded background queue owned by each EngineCore.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import queue
+import threading
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from contextlib import suppress
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import msgspec
+import zmq
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.v1.metrics.iteration import ITERATION_TIMING_SCOPE
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+    from vllm.v1.metrics.stats import SchedulerIterationDetails
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+FPM_VERSION = 1
+FPM_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE = 10_000
+FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA = ITERATION_TIMING_SCOPE
+
+
+class ScheduledRequestMetrics(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Requests scheduled in one model execution."""
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    # Population variance of kv_read + scheduled_tokens / 2, in tokens squared.
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    sum_prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+class QueuedRequestMetrics(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Waiting work at the iteration record's queue-snapshot boundary."""
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+class ForwardPassMetrics(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Versioned, per-iteration forward-pass metrics wire payload."""
+
+    version: int = FPM_VERSION
+    worker_id: str = ""
+    dp_rank: int = 0
+    counter_id: int = 0
+    timing_scope: str = FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA
+    # CUDA-stream interval in seconds; zero denotes engine-confirmed idle.
+    wall_time: float = 0.0
+    scheduled_requests: ScheduledRequestMetrics = ScheduledRequestMetrics()
+    queued_requests: QueuedRequestMetrics = QueuedRequestMetrics()
+
+
+_fpm_encoder = msgspec.msgpack.Encoder()
+_fpm_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(ForwardPassMetrics)
+
+
+def encode_forward_pass_metrics(metrics: ForwardPassMetrics) -> bytes:
+    return _fpm_encoder.encode(metrics)
+
+
+def decode_forward_pass_metrics(data: bytes) -> ForwardPassMetrics | None:
+    """Decode an FPM payload, ignoring malformed or unsupported versions."""
+    try:
+        metrics = _fpm_decoder.decode(data)
+    except msgspec.DecodeError:
+        logger.warning("Ignoring malformed forward-pass metrics payload")
+        return None
+    if metrics.version != FPM_VERSION:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Ignoring forward-pass metrics version %d; supported version is %d",
+            metrics.version,
+            FPM_VERSION,
+        )
+        return None
+    return metrics
+
+
+def forward_pass_metrics_from_iteration(
+    details: SchedulerIterationDetails,
+    worker_id: str,
+    dp_rank: int,
+    sequence: int,
+) -> ForwardPassMetrics | None:
+    """Map one complete record without recomputing its workload or timing."""
+    scheduled = details.scheduled_workload
+    queued = details.queued_workload
+    if (
+        details.elapsed_ms is None
+        or details.timing_scope != FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA
+        or scheduled is None
+        or queued is None
+        or (details.elapsed_ms <= 0 and not details.is_idle)
+    ):
+        logger.warning_once("Skipping incomplete or untimed forward-pass metrics")
+        return None
+    return ForwardPassMetrics(
+        worker_id=worker_id,
+        dp_rank=dp_rank,
+        counter_id=sequence,
+        wall_time=details.elapsed_ms * 1e-3,
+        scheduled_requests=ScheduledRequestMetrics(
+            num_prefill_requests=details.num_ctx_requests,
+            sum_prefill_tokens=details.num_ctx_tokens,
+            var_prefill_length=scheduled.var_prefill_length,
+            sum_prefill_kv_tokens=scheduled.sum_prefill_kv_tokens,
+            num_decode_requests=details.num_generation_requests,
+            sum_decode_kv_tokens=scheduled.sum_decode_kv_tokens,
+            var_decode_kv_tokens=scheduled.var_decode_kv_tokens,
+        ),
+        queued_requests=QueuedRequestMetrics(
+            num_prefill_requests=queued.num_prefill_requests,
+            sum_prefill_tokens=queued.sum_prefill_tokens,
+            var_prefill_length=queued.var_prefill_length,
+            num_decode_requests=queued.num_decode_requests,
+            sum_decode_kv_tokens=queued.sum_decode_kv_tokens,
+            var_decode_kv_tokens=queued.var_decode_kv_tokens,
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+class ForwardPassMetricsExporter:
+    """Non-blocking exporter; one background thread owns this engine's socket."""
+
+    SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1.0
+    STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0
+
+    def __init__(self, base_port: int, worker_id: str, dp_rank: int) -> None:
+        self._base_port = base_port
+        self._worker_id = worker_id
+        self._dp_rank = dp_rank
+        self._queue: queue.Queue[tuple[int, SchedulerIterationDetails] | None] = (
+            queue.Queue(maxsize=FPM_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE)
+        )
+        self._sequence = 0
+        self._stop = threading.Event()
+        self._ready = threading.Event()
+        self._startup_error: Exception | None = None
+        self._thread = threading.Thread(
+            target=self._run, daemon=True, name="fpm-zmq-publisher"
+        )
+        self._thread.start()
+        if not self._ready.wait(self.STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):
+            self.shutdown()
+            raise TimeoutError("Timed out binding forward-pass metrics publisher")
+        if self._startup_error is not None:
+            self.shutdown()
+            raise RuntimeError("Failed to bind forward-pass metrics publisher") from (
+                self._startup_error
+            )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_vllm_config(
+        cls, vllm_config: VllmConfig
+    ) -> ForwardPassMetricsExporter | None:
+        config = vllm_config.observability_config
+        if config.forward_pass_metrics_port == 0:
+            return None
+        return cls(
+            config.forward_pass_metrics_port,
+            config.forward_pass_metrics_worker_id or vllm_config.instance_id,
+            vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_index,
+        )
+
+    def record(self, records: Sequence[SchedulerIterationDetails]) -> None:
+        if self._stop.is_set():
+            return
+        for details in records:
+            sequence = self._sequence
+            self._sequence += 1
+            try:
+                self._queue.put_nowait((sequence, details))
+            except queue.Full:
+                logger.warning_once(
+                    "Forward-pass metrics queue is full; dropping samples"
+                )
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        self._stop.set()
+        with suppress(queue.Full):
+            self._queue.put_nowait(None)
+        self._thread.join(timeout=self.SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
+        if self._thread.is_alive():
+            logger.warning("Forward-pass metrics publisher did not stop in time")
+
+    def _bind_socket(self) -> zmq.Socket:
+        port = self._base_port + self._dp_rank
+        if not 1 <= port <= 65535:
+            raise ValueError("forward-pass-metrics-port plus DP rank exceeds TCP range")
+        endpoint = f"tcp://*:{port}"
+        socket = zmq.Context.instance().socket(zmq.PUB)
+        try:
+            socket.bind(endpoint)
+        except Exception:
+            socket.close(linger=0)
+            raise
+        logger.info("Forward-pass metrics publisher bound to %s", endpoint)
+        return socket
+
+    def _run(self) -> None:
+        socket: zmq.Socket | None = None
+        try:
+            try:
+                socket = self._bind_socket()
+            except Exception as exc:
+                self._startup_error = exc
+                return
+            finally:
+                self._ready.set()
+            while not self._stop.is_set():
+                item = self._queue.get()
+                if item is None:
+                    break
+                sequence, details = item
+                metrics = forward_pass_metrics_from_iteration(
+                    details, self._worker_id, self._dp_rank, sequence
+                )
+                if metrics is None:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    socket.send_multipart(
+                        (
+                            b"",
+                            sequence.to_bytes(8, "big"),
+                            encode_forward_pass_metrics(metrics),
+                        ),
+                        flags=zmq.NOBLOCK,
+                    )
+                except zmq.Again:
+                    logger.warning_once("Forward-pass metrics send queue is full")
+                except Exception as exc:
+                    logger.warning_once("Forward-pass metrics publish failed: %s", exc)
+        finally:
+            if socket is not None:
+                socket.close(linger=0)

+"""Associate scheduled batches with asynchronously completed worker timings."""

+from __future__ import annotations

+ITERATION_TIMING_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.005

+# it does not bound total engine shutdown or guarantee frontend delivery.
+ITERATION_TIMING_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 1.0

+                "Iteration workload metrics require scheduler.requests"
+            )
+            assert scheduler.waiting is not None, (
+                "Iteration workload metrics require scheduler.waiting"
+            )
+            assert scheduler.kv_holding_waiting is not None, (
+                "Iteration workload metrics require scheduler.kv_holding_waiting"
+            )
+        self._scheduler = scheduler
+        self._correct_async_spec_lengths = (
+            scheduler is not None and correct_async_spec_lengths
+        )

+        # association until both output processing and timing have completed.
+        self._pending: dict[int, _PendingIteration] = {}
+        self._ready: list[SchedulerIterationDetails] = []

+            assert self._scheduler is not None
+            requests = self._scheduler.requests
+            assert requests is not None

+                rid: (request, request.num_preemptions)
+                for rid in output.num_scheduled_tokens

+            counts = IterationDetails(
+                num_ctx_requests=workload.num_prefill_requests,
+                num_ctx_tokens=workload.num_prefill_tokens,

+
+    def complete_timing_samples(self, samples: tuple[tuple[int, float], ...]) -> None:
+        for iteration_id, elapsed_ms in samples:
+            pending = self._pending.get(iteration_id)
+            if pending is not None:
+                pending.details.elapsed_ms = elapsed_ms
+                self._complete_if_ready(iteration_id)
+
+    def _complete_if_ready(self, iteration_id: int) -> None:
+        pending = self._pending[iteration_id]

+            self._ready.append(pending.details)
+            del self._pending[iteration_id]
+
+    def take_ready(self) -> list[SchedulerIterationDetails]:
+        ready, self._ready = self._ready, []
+        return ready
+
+    def has_pending_timing(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self._pending) or self._timing_poll is not None
+
+    def _receive_ready_timing(self) -> None:
+        if self._timing_poll is not None:
+            samples = self._timing_poll()
+            if samples is None:
+                return
+            self._timing_poll = None
+            self.complete_timing_samples(samples)
+
+    def poll_timing(self, executor: Executor) -> None:
+        self._receive_ready_timing()
+        if self._timing_poll is not None:
+            return
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if not self._pending or now < self._next_timing_poll:
+            return
+        self._next_timing_poll = now + ITERATION_TIMING_POLL_INTERVAL
+        self._timing_poll = executor.start_iteration_timing_poll()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Nonblocking GPU iteration timing shared by both model runners.
+
+Intervals span model execution, sampling and speculative drafting on the
+recorded stream, including host-submission gaps. Independent work on other
+streams and EngineCore scheduling are outside this timing scope.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import queue
+import threading
+from collections import deque
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from copy import copy
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class _PendingTiming:
+    iteration_id: int
+    start_event: Any
+    end_event: Any
+
+
+class IterationTimer:
+    """Pool timing events and collect only completed GPU intervals.
+
+    Output-copy and worker threads may drain concurrently. A contended drain
+    returns immediately instead of delaying the next model execution.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_event_pairs: int,
+        event_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        if num_event_pairs <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("num_event_pairs must be positive")
+        self._event_factory = event_factory or self._make_event
+        self._event_pool: queue.SimpleQueue[tuple[Any, Any]] = queue.SimpleQueue()
+        for _ in range(num_event_pairs):
+            self._event_pool.put((self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()))
+        self._pending: deque[_PendingTiming] = deque()
+        self._active: _PendingTiming | None = None
+        self._drain_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _make_event() -> torch.Event:
+        return torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
+
+    def start(self, iteration_id: int | None) -> None:
+        if self._active is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("An iteration timing interval is already active")
+        if iteration_id is None:
+            return
+        try:
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_pool.get_nowait()
+        except queue.Empty:
+            # DP dummy steps can outlive the ordinary batch-queue bound.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Iteration CUDA event pool exhausted; allocating one extra pair"
+            )
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()
+        start_event.record()
+        self._active = _PendingTiming(iteration_id, start_event, end_event)
+
+    def finish(self) -> None:
+        if self._active is None:
+            return
+        pending = self._active
+        self._active = None
+        pending.end_event.record()
+        self._pending.append(pending)
+
+    def cancel(self) -> None:
+        # Discard this pair instead of recycling an event still in flight.
+        self._active = None
+
+    def drain_samples(self) -> tuple[tuple[int, float], ...]:
+        """Return ready (iteration_id, elapsed_ms) pairs without synchronization."""
+        if not self._drain_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+            return ()
+        ready: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
+        try:
+            while self._pending:
+                # The producer only appends; _drain_lock keeps this head stable.
+                pending = self._pending[0]
+                if not pending.end_event.query():
+                    break
+
+                elapsed_ms = pending.start_event.elapsed_time(pending.end_event)
+                self._pending.popleft()
+                ready.append((pending.iteration_id, elapsed_ms))
+                self._event_pool.put((pending.start_event, pending.end_event))
+        finally:
+            self._drain_lock.release()
+        return tuple(ready)
+
+    def drain_into(self, output: Any) -> Any:
+        """Attach ready samples without mutating shared empty runner outputs.
+
+        Async handles collect their samples later in get_output().
+        """
+        if output is None or not hasattr(output, "iteration_timing_samples"):
+            return output
+        ready = self.drain_samples()
+        if not ready:
+            return output
+        output = copy(output)
+        output.iteration_timing_samples += ready
+        return output
+
+
+def make_iteration_timer(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    rank: int,
+) -> IterationTimer | None:
+    """Allocate events only when timing is enabled on the model-output rank."""
+    if not vllm_config.observability_config.iteration_timing_enabled:
+        return None
+    parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    output_rank = parallel_config.world_size - (
+        parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size
+        * parallel_config.prefill_context_parallel_size
+    )
+    if rank != output_rank:
+        return None
+    return IterationTimer(num_event_pairs=vllm_config.max_concurrent_batches + 1)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Transport-independent workload snapshots for completed engine iterations."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from itertools import chain
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import WelfordAccumulator
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.core.sched.interface import SchedulerInterface
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScheduledIterationWorkload:
+    """Logical context lengths at the start of the scheduled model execution."""
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    num_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    num_decode_tokens: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    # Population variance of kv_read + scheduled_tokens / 2, in tokens squared.
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class QueuedIterationWorkload:
+    """Waiting work after output processing, or at dummy/idle submission.
+
+    Preempted requests and requests waiting for remote KV are grouped as
+    queued decode work. This queue category is distinct from the scheduler's
+    execution phase: a resumed request may need prefill recomputation.
+    """
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class IterationWorkloadAccumulator:
+    prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    decode_tokens: int = 0
+    prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    prefill_lengths: WelfordAccumulator = field(default_factory=WelfordAccumulator)
+    decode_lengths: WelfordAccumulator = field(default_factory=WelfordAccumulator)
+
+    def add_prefill(self, kv_tokens: int, scheduled_tokens: int) -> None:
+        self.prefill_tokens += scheduled_tokens
+        self.prefill_kv_tokens += kv_tokens
+        # Keep half-token attention lengths exact during integer accumulation.
+        self.prefill_lengths.add(2 * kv_tokens + scheduled_tokens)
+
+    def add_decode(self, kv_tokens: int, scheduled_tokens: int) -> None:
+        self.decode_tokens += scheduled_tokens
+        self.decode_lengths.add(kv_tokens)
+
+    def snapshot(self) -> ScheduledIterationWorkload:
+        return ScheduledIterationWorkload(
+            num_prefill_requests=self.prefill_lengths.count,
+            num_prefill_tokens=self.prefill_tokens,
+            num_decode_requests=self.decode_lengths.count,
+            num_decode_tokens=self.decode_tokens,
+            sum_prefill_kv_tokens=self.prefill_kv_tokens,
+            var_prefill_length=self.prefill_lengths.variance / 4,
+            sum_decode_kv_tokens=self.decode_lengths.total,
+            var_decode_kv_tokens=self.decode_lengths.variance,
+        )
+
+
+def extract_queued_workload(scheduler: "SchedulerInterface") -> QueuedIterationWorkload:
+    from vllm.v1.request import RequestStatus
+
+    waiting = scheduler.waiting
+    kv_holding_waiting = scheduler.kv_holding_waiting
+    assert waiting is not None
+    assert kv_holding_waiting is not None
+    prefill = WelfordAccumulator()
+    decode = WelfordAccumulator()
+    # Deferred requests are already in these disjoint queues.
+    for request in chain(waiting, kv_holding_waiting):
+        if request.status in (
+            RequestStatus.PREEMPTED,
+            RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS,
+        ):
+            decode.add(request.num_computed_tokens)
+        else:
+            prefill.add(request.num_tokens)
+    return QueuedIterationWorkload(
+        num_prefill_requests=prefill.count,
+        sum_prefill_tokens=prefill.total,
+        var_prefill_length=prefill.variance,
+        num_decode_requests=decode.count,
+        sum_decode_kv_tokens=decode.total,
+        var_decode_kv_tokens=decode.variance,
+    )

+import threading
+import time
+from collections import OrderedDict, deque

+FPM_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 1.0
+FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA = "model_step_cuda"
+

+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class WelfordAccumulator:
+    """Single-pass count, sum, and population variance accumulator."""
+
+    count: int = 0
+    total: int = 0
+    _mean: float = 0.0
+    _m2: float = 0.0
+
+    def add(self, value: int) -> None:
+        self.count += 1
+        self.total += value
+        delta = value - self._mean
+        self._mean += delta / self.count
+        self._m2 += delta * (value - self._mean)
+
+    @property
+    def variance(self) -> float:
+        return self._m2 / self.count if self.count else 0.0
+
+
+class ScheduledRequestMetrics(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Requests scheduled in one model execution."""
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    sum_prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+

+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Requests waiting after one model execution completes."""
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0

+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]

+
+    version: int = FPM_VERSION
+    worker_id: str = ""
+    dp_rank: int = 0
+    counter_id: int = 0
+    timing_scope: str = FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA
+    # CUDA-timeline interval spanning execution, sampling and drafting, in seconds.
+    wall_time: float = 0.0
+    scheduled_requests: ScheduledRequestMetrics = ScheduledRequestMetrics()
+    queued_requests: QueuedRequestMetrics = QueuedRequestMetrics()
+
+
+_fpm_encoder = msgspec.msgpack.Encoder()
+_fpm_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(ForwardPassMetrics)
+

+    return _fpm_encoder.encode(metrics)

+
+def decode_forward_pass_metrics(data: bytes) -> ForwardPassMetrics | None:
+    """Decode an FPM payload, returning ``None`` for unsupported versions."""
+
+    try:
+        metrics = _fpm_decoder.decode(data)
+    except msgspec.DecodeError:
+        logger.warning("Ignoring malformed forward-pass metrics payload")
+        return None
+    if metrics.version != FPM_VERSION:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Ignoring forward-pass metrics version %d; supported version is %d",
+            metrics.version,
+            FPM_VERSION,
+        )
+        return None

+@dataclass(slots=True)

+class ForwardPassMetricsTimer:
+    """Non-blocking CUDA event timer used by both GPU model runners.
+
+    Timing events are preallocated and pooled. Hot-path drains only read elapsed
+    time after ``query`` reports completion. The engine uses ``wait=True`` only
+    on the cold transition to idle so the final iteration cannot be lost.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_event_pairs: int,
+        event_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        if num_event_pairs <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("num_event_pairs must be positive")
+        self._event_factory = event_factory or self._make_event
+        self._event_pool: queue.SimpleQueue[tuple[Any, Any]] = queue.SimpleQueue()
+        for _ in range(num_event_pairs):
+            self._event_pool.put((self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()))
+        self._pending: deque[_PendingTiming] = deque()
+        self._active: _PendingTiming | None = None
+        self._pending_lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._drain_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _make_event() -> torch.cuda.Event:
+        return torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)

+    def start(self, scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput) -> None:
+        if self._active is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("A forward-pass timing interval is already active")

+        if iteration_id is None or scheduler_output.total_num_scheduled_tokens == 0:
+            return
+        try:
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_pool.get_nowait()
+        except queue.Empty:
+            # This should only be possible if the configured concurrency bound
+            # is violated or completed events are not being drained.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Forward-pass CUDA event pool exhausted; allocating one extra pair"
+            )
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()
+        start_event.record()
+        self._active = _PendingTiming(iteration_id, start_event, end_event)
+
+    def finish(self) -> None:
+        if self._active is None:
+            return
+        pending = self._active
+        self._active = None
+        pending.end_event.record()
+        with self._pending_lock:
+            self._pending.append(pending)
+
+    def cancel(self) -> None:
+        # Exception paths are cold. Wait before recycling the recorded start
+        # event so a later interval cannot re-record it while it is in flight.
+        if self._active is not None:
+            self._active.start_event.synchronize()
+            self._event_pool.put((self._active.start_event, self._active.end_event))
+        self._active = None
+
+    def drain_samples(self, wait: bool = False) -> tuple[tuple[int, float], ...]:
+        """Return completed timing samples without blocking unless requested.
+
+        CUDA driver calls run outside ``_pending_lock``. The inference thread
+        therefore never waits behind ``query``/``elapsed_time``/``synchronize``.
+        """
+
+        ready: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
+        with self._drain_lock:
+            while True:
+                with self._pending_lock:
+                    pending = self._pending[0] if self._pending else None
+                if pending is None:
+                    break
+                if wait:
+                    pending.end_event.synchronize()
+                elif not pending.end_event.query():
+                    break
+
+                elapsed_ms = pending.start_event.elapsed_time(pending.end_event)
+                with self._pending_lock:
+                    completed = self._pending.popleft()
+                assert completed is pending
+                ready.append((pending.iteration_id, elapsed_ms * 1e-3))
+                self._event_pool.put((pending.start_event, pending.end_event))
+        return tuple(ready)
+
+    def drain_into(self, output: Any) -> Any:
+        """Attach ready timing samples to a model-runner output."""
+
+        if output is None or not hasattr(output, "forward_pass_timing_samples"):
+            return output
+        ready = self.drain_samples()
+        if not ready:
+            return output
+
+        # EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT is a shared singleton. Copy every output
+        # before attaching samples so instrumentation cannot mutate shared state.
+        output = copy(output)
+        output.forward_pass_timing_samples += ready
+        return output

+
+def make_forward_pass_metrics_timer(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    is_output_rank: bool,

+    The disabled path allocates no CUDA events and model runners only execute
+    one predictable Python branch in existing worker methods.

+        vllm_config.observability_config.forward_pass_metrics_port <= 0
+        or not is_output_rank
+    ):

+

+        if self._startup_error is not None:

+            ) from self._startup_error

+            self._queue.put_nowait(metrics)
+        except queue.Full:
+            # FPM is observability data and must never backpressure inference.
+            logger.warning_once("Forward-pass metrics queue is full; dropping samples")
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        self._stop.set()
+        with suppress(queue.Full):
+            self._queue.put_nowait(None)
+        self._thread.join(timeout=self.SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
+        if self._thread.is_alive():
+            logger.warning("Forward-pass metrics publisher did not stop in time")
+
+    def _run(self) -> None:
+        socket: zmq.Socket[bytes] | None = None

Thanks for pointing this out. This was a pending FPM schema-semantics issue we had not fixed yet: the scheduled prefill variance should describe attention lengths for this iteration, rather than the full original prompt lengths.

Fixed in eddd3b427b. For each scheduled prefill request with x cached/read KV tokens and y tokens to compute in this iteration, we use x + y/2, and report the unweighted population variance across those requests. For chunked prefill, y is only this chunk's scheduled query length; future chunks are excluded. sum_prefill_tokens still sums y, and sum_prefill_kv_tokens still sums x.

The regression uses attention lengths 4 + 1/2 and 2 + 3/2 (variance 0.25), including an original 1000-token prompt, to distinguish this from full-prompt or query-only variance and verify half-token precision. The v1 field name is retained. Queued metrics continue to describe waiting requests, not an executed iteration.

The in-tree Scheduler and AsyncScheduler do share these fields. The reason for the getter is that EngineCore accepts SchedulerInterface/custom scheduler implementations, and these attributes are not part of that interface. FPM needs the requests lookup (not just running) to track request identity and preemption generation for async speculative rejection corrections, plus waiting and skipped_waiting for queue metrics.

I kept the narrow getter to make that dependency explicit and fail clearly at startup for a custom scheduler that enables FPM without providing the state. With the prefill variance correction, scheduled prefill aggregates now come entirely from SchedulerOutput; the lookup is only needed for async SD correction and queue state. +logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+FPM_VERSION = 1
+FPM_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 1.0
+FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA = "model_step_cuda"

+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class WelfordAccumulator:
+    """Single-pass count, sum, and population variance accumulator."""
+
+    count: int = 0
+    total: int = 0
+    _mean: float = 0.0
+    _m2: float = 0.0
+
+    def add(self, value: int) -> None:
+        self.count += 1
+        self.total += value
+        delta = value - self._mean
+        self._mean += delta / self.count
+        self._m2 += delta * (value - self._mean)
+
+    @property
+    def variance(self) -> float:
+        return self._m2 / self.count if self.count else 0.0
+
+
+class ScheduledRequestMetrics(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Requests scheduled in one model execution."""
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    sum_prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+class QueuedRequestMetrics(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Requests waiting after one model execution completes."""
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0

+class ForwardPassMetrics(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    frozen=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+):
+    """Versioned, per-iteration forward-pass metrics wire payload."""
+
+    version: int = FPM_VERSION
+    worker_id: str = ""
+    dp_rank: int = 0
+    counter_id: int = 0
+    timing_scope: str = FPM_TIMING_SCOPE_MODEL_STEP_CUDA
+    # CUDA-timeline interval spanning execution, sampling and drafting, in seconds.
+    wall_time: float = 0.0
+    scheduled_requests: ScheduledRequestMetrics = ScheduledRequestMetrics()
+    queued_requests: QueuedRequestMetrics = QueuedRequestMetrics()
+
+
+_fpm_encoder = msgspec.msgpack.Encoder()
+_fpm_decoder = msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(ForwardPassMetrics)
+
+
+def encode_forward_pass_metrics(metrics: ForwardPassMetrics) -> bytes:
+    return _fpm_encoder.encode(metrics)
+
+
+def decode_forward_pass_metrics(data: bytes) -> ForwardPassMetrics | None:
+    """Decode an FPM payload, returning ``None`` for unsupported versions."""
+
+    try:
+        metrics = _fpm_decoder.decode(data)
+    except msgspec.DecodeError:
+        logger.warning("Ignoring malformed forward-pass metrics payload")
+        return None
+    if metrics.version != FPM_VERSION:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Ignoring forward-pass metrics version %d; supported version is %d",
+            metrics.version,
+            FPM_VERSION,
+        )
+        return None
+    return metrics
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class _PendingTiming:
+    iteration_id: int
+    start_event: Any
+    end_event: Any
+
+
+class ForwardPassMetricsTimer:
+    """Non-blocking CUDA event timer used by both GPU model runners.
+
+    Timing events are preallocated and pooled. Hot-path drains only read elapsed
+    time after ``query`` reports completion. The engine uses ``wait=True`` only
+    on the cold transition to idle so the final iteration cannot be lost.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_event_pairs: int,
+        event_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        if num_event_pairs <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("num_event_pairs must be positive")
+        self._event_factory = event_factory or self._make_event
+        self._event_pool: queue.SimpleQueue[tuple[Any, Any]] = queue.SimpleQueue()
+        for _ in range(num_event_pairs):
+            self._event_pool.put((self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()))
+        self._pending: deque[_PendingTiming] = deque()
+        self._active: _PendingTiming | None = None
+        self._pending_lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._drain_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _make_event() -> torch.cuda.Event:
+        return torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+
+    def start(self, scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput) -> None:
+        if self._active is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("A forward-pass timing interval is already active")
+        iteration_id = scheduler_output.forward_pass_metrics_iteration_id
+        if iteration_id is None or scheduler_output.total_num_scheduled_tokens == 0:
+            return
+        try:
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_pool.get_nowait()
+        except queue.Empty:
+            # This should only be possible if the configured concurrency bound
+            # is violated or completed events are not being drained.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Forward-pass CUDA event pool exhausted; allocating one extra pair"
+            )
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()
+        start_event.record()
+        self._active = _PendingTiming(iteration_id, start_event, end_event)
+
+    def finish(self) -> None:
+        if self._active is None:
+            return
+        pending = self._active
+        self._active = None
+        pending.end_event.record()
+        with self._pending_lock:
+            self._pending.append(pending)
+
+    def cancel(self) -> None:
+        # Exception paths are cold. Wait before recycling the recorded start
+        # event so a later interval cannot re-record it while it is in flight.
+        if self._active is not None:
+            self._active.start_event.synchronize()
+            self._event_pool.put((self._active.start_event, self._active.end_event))
+        self._active = None
+
+    def drain_samples(self, wait: bool = False) -> tuple[tuple[int, float], ...]:
+        """Return completed timing samples without blocking unless requested.
+
+        CUDA driver calls run outside ``_pending_lock``. The inference thread
+        therefore never waits behind ``query``/``elapsed_time``/``synchronize``.
+        """
+
+        ready: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
+        with self._drain_lock:
+            while True:
+                with self._pending_lock:
+                    pending = self._pending[0] if self._pending else None
+                if pending is None:
+                    break
+                if wait:
+                    pending.end_event.synchronize()
+                elif not pending.end_event.query():
+                    break
+
+                elapsed_ms = pending.start_event.elapsed_time(pending.end_event)
+                with self._pending_lock:
+                    completed = self._pending.popleft()
+                assert completed is pending
+                ready.append((pending.iteration_id, elapsed_ms * 1e-3))
+                self._event_pool.put((pending.start_event, pending.end_event))
+        return tuple(ready)
+
+    def drain_into(self, output: Any) -> Any:
+        """Attach ready timing samples to a model-runner output."""
+
+        if output is None or not hasattr(output, "forward_pass_timing_samples"):
+            return output
+        ready = self.drain_samples()
+        if not ready:
+            return output
+
+        # EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT is a shared singleton. Copy every output
+        # before attaching samples so instrumentation cannot mutate shared state.
+        output = copy(output)
+        output.forward_pass_timing_samples += ready
+        return output
+
+
+def make_forward_pass_metrics_timer(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    is_output_rank: bool,
+) -> ForwardPassMetricsTimer | None:
+    """Create a preallocated timer only on the model-output worker.
+
+    The disabled path allocates no CUDA events and model runners only execute
+    one predictable Python branch in existing worker methods.
+    """
+
+    if (
+        vllm_config.observability_config.forward_pass_metrics_port <= 0
+        or not is_output_rank
+    ):
+        return None
+    return ForwardPassMetricsTimer(
+        num_event_pairs=max(2, vllm_config.max_concurrent_batches + 1)
+    )
+
+
+def is_forward_pass_metrics_output_rank(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    rank: int,
+) -> bool:
+    """Return whether ``rank`` owns the executor's ModelRunnerOutput."""
+
+    parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    output_rank = parallel_config.world_size - (
+        parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size
+        * parallel_config.prefill_context_parallel_size
+    )
+    return rank == output_rank
+
